title: Classic Pizza
subtitle: with a slow-rise dough and fresh tomato sauce
description: Homemade pizza dough and a simple tomato and garlic sauce, baked on a very hot stone or inverted tray. The dough makes four 28 cm pizzas, and partly baked bases freeze well.

steps.text: Pour the water into a mixer bowl and crumble in the yeast. Sift in the flour and knead with the dough hook on low for 2 minutes. Add the salt and sugar, increase to medium and knead for 10 more minutes until soft and pliable.

Shape the dough into a ball, place in a bowl lightly oiled with olive oil, cover and leave to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled. Place a baking stone (or an inverted tray) in the oven and heat to the highest setting (250°C).
Fold the dough in the bowl like an envelope, flip it seam side down, cover and rise for another 20 minutes. Divide into 4 equal pieces, shape into balls, cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Make the sauce: fry the crushed garlic in the olive oil for a few seconds until fragrant but not browned. Add the chopped tomatoes and sugar and cook on medium heat for 7 minutes to thicken (10 minutes more if using canned tomatoes). Season with salt and pepper.
Roll each ball to a 14 cm round, then stretch gently over your fists to about 40 cm. Place on baking paper dusted with durum flour.
Spread with tomato sauce and add toppings and cheese. Slide onto the hot stone using the baking paper and bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
